The strongest ground is that the promise was oral. Many states require a signed writing to revive a debt that the statute of limitations has barred, so the oral promise is unenforceable there, and that rule is stronger than a consideration argument. Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 82 would make the promise binding without a writing, so the answer depends on the jurisdiction's revival rule. The overheard "deadbeat" remark neither supplies consideration nor creates duress.

CONFIDENCE: 65
